title: What is the next dot picture in each of seven sequences?
description: Seven sequences are drawn as dot pictures. The video draws the sixth picture of each by adding the same kind of piece again, and checks the triangular picture by its rows.
teaching_notes: One idea: to draw the next picture, find the piece that each picture added to the one before, and add it again. Watch for students who draw the next picture without checking its count.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (Math Talk), p.5
video_script.why: The child draws the next picture of seven dot sequences by adding the piece that each earlier picture added.
video_script.substitution: Find the piece each picture added, and add it once more.
video_script.anchor: seven rows of dot pictures from the book, each with five pictures drawn and one empty frame at the end
video_script.payoff_line: Each sequence grows by its own kind of piece

final_answer.value: Next pictures: All 1's: 1 dot; Counting: 6 dots in a row; Odd: 11 dots; Even: 12 dots (two rows of 6); Triangular: 21 dots (triangle of 6 rows); Squares: 36 dots (6 by 6 grid); Cubes: 216 unit blocks (6 x 6 x 6 cube).
final_answer.spoken: each sequence grows by its own kind of piece, and the sixth picture shows it

hold_back: Each sequence grows by its own kind of piece
never_show: draw the next picture without counting
maths_rules: all ones: one more single dot
counting numbers: the sixth picture is 6 dots in a row
odd numbers: the sixth odd number is 11, so 11 dots
even numbers: the sixth even number is 12, so 12 dots in two rows of 6
triangular: add a sixth row of 6 dots, 15 + 6 = 21 dots
squares: a 6 by 6 grid, 6 x 6 = 36 dots
cubes: a 6 by 6 by 6 cube, 6 x 6 x 6 = 216 blocks
video_script.design: One idea: the next picture adds the same kind of piece. Callback to the picture that adds a column of dots. Wrong idea: none is broken. The seven rows stay on the board to the end.
